question: Záhradkári zakopú do záhona pohárik až po okraj a nalejú doň obyčajný nápoj. Slizniaky ho zacítia, vlezú dnu a utopia sa. Aký nápoj to je?
source_excerpt: Zakopte nádobu tak, aby bola zarovno s pôdou

extra.why_interesting: Many Slovaks have seen a cup buried in a neighbour's vegetable patch without knowing why. Players can reason toward the answer from the clue that the drink has a strong smell. The payoff is that slugs are drawn to the yeast in beer.
extra.verification_notes: Beer-filled buried cup is the standard slug trap described by Slovak/Czech gardening sources; other liquids exist but beer is the canonical answer (https://www.arecenze.cz/clanky/pivni-past-na-slimaky-a-vosy/).

explanation: Slizniaky priťahuje vôňa kvasníc. Pre nich pivo vonia ako hnijúce rastliny, ich obľúbená potrava, takže sa za ňou plazia aj z niekoľkých metrov.

question: Krt si pod zemou zakladá špajzu so zásobami na horšie časy. Aké zvieratá si do nej ukladá, a to ešte živé?
source_excerpt: When earthworms are plentiful, during autumn and winter, the mole makes stores of them, biting off their heads and pushing them into the ground for eating later.

extra.why_interesting: Every Slovak knows the friendly cartoon Krtko and has seen molehills in gardens, but few imagine a mole keeping a pantry. Players can work out the answer from what moles eat underground. The macabre detail about how the food is kept alive is the delight.
extra.verification_notes: Moles store paralysed, still-living earthworms in underground larders (YPTE mole factsheet, https://ypte.org.uk/factsheets/mole/food-and-feeding); the answer 'dážďovky' is correct.

explanation: Krt dážďovkám prehryzne prednú časť tela, takže ochrnú, ale zostanú živé a čerstvé. V jednej krtej špajzi našli aj vyše tisíc dážďoviek.
